claims.head: Like for like: Formenton against Copp
claims.call: The Oilers’ L3 (Formenton, Michaels and Joseph) spends at least 38% of its 5-on-5 time against the Red Wings’ third line.
claims.body: At home, the Oilers keep sending Formenton’s line (Formenton, Michaels and Joseph) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Mike Babcock keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Red Wings’ third line is Rasmussen, Compher and Copp.
claims.nums: At home: 38% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against third lines, about 21% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Mike Babcock likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Red Wings’ third line.
claims.cite: Matchups · Edmonton home games this season · 5 games, 44 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

chips.tip: Edmonton’s L3 (Formenton, Michaels and Joseph) at home: 38% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ third lines. Matchups, Edmonton home games this season, 5 games, 44 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face third lines about 21% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

claims.head: Penalties could cost the Red Wings
claims.call: The Oilers’ power play creates at least their usual 9.8 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Oilers’ power play is the league’s best, and the Red Wings’ kill is near the bottom. Every trip to the box hurts the Red Wings more than most. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.

notes.text: Simon Edvinsson has not played this season. He is a top-pair defenseman. Ben Chiarot has taken his spot beside Moritz Seider.
Michal Postava was added to the roster on Oct 23.
Mattias Ekholm is out, reported after he played in their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Matt Savoie is on long-term injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has not played this season. Leon Draisaitl has taken his spot beside Connor McDavid and Vasily Podkolzin.
Ryan Nugent-Hopkins returned in their last game after missing 9 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 50% of the team’s power-play time in 10 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 2% of the team’s shorthanded time in 8 games, down from 30% last season.

EDM.head: Advantage, the Oilers
EDM.body: Even though Edmonton will be without Ekholm, the Oilers have been out-chancing opponents lately and have home-ice advantage. The Red Wings’ way back in is a power play that gets going.

DET.head: Not an easy night for the Red Wings
DET.body: Even though Edmonton will be without Ekholm, the Oilers have been out-chancing opponents lately and have home-ice advantage. The Red Wings can pull it off if their power play gets going.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Red Wings?
paras: The Oilers have won three straight. The Red Wings are 4-3-3.

items.text: The Red Wings have been without Simon Edvinsson all season.
The Oilers are newly without Mattias Ekholm, and have had to make do without Matt Savoie all season.
Leon Draisaitl has a point in five straight games against Detroit, and 9 points in his last six against them.
Connor McDavid has a point in every game this season.
